display.purpose: Section-level headings in the staff dashboard and select public sections. Rare by design.

hero.purpose: The public homepage hero headline only.

mono.purpose: Loaded but not yet visibly used; reserved for code/data-dense contexts.

shadows.name: shadow-mini
shadows.purpose: Subtle elevation: inputs, inline chips, small cards.

shadows.name: shadow-popover
shadows.purpose: Floating elements: dropdowns, modals, tooltips; elevated card variant.

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: #18181b; color: #ffffff; border-radius: 5px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #18181be6; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff, 0 0 0 4px #18181b; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary bordered button, used against dark or light hero backgrounds.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: #ffffff; color: #18181b; border: 1px solid #18181b; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 32px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #ededed; }

components.name: Default Card
components.html: Here is the content of the card that needs to be displayed
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; color: #171717; border: 1px solid rgba(24,24,27,0.1); border-radius: 16px; padding: 24px; box-shadow: 0px 2px 0px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.04); transition: box-shadow 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-card--interactive:hover { box-shadow: 0px 7px 12px 3px rgba(24,24,27,0.1); transform: scale(1.02); cursor: pointer; } .ds-card--interactive:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Floating-Label Input
components.description: Text input with an animated floating label, used across auth and booking forms.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; width: 100%; } .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 24px 44px 12px 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(24,24,27,0.17); border-radius: 9px; background: #ffffff; font-size: 16px; color: #171717; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: rgba(24,24,27,0.4); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff, 0 0 0 4px #18181b; } .ds-input-label { position: absolute; left: 16px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); font-weight: 500; color: #525252; transition: all 0.2s ease-in-out; transform-origin: top left; } .ds-input:focus + .ds-input-label, .ds-input:not(:placeholder-shown) + .ds-input-label { transform: translateY(-1.6125rem) scale(0.8); color: rgba(23,23,23,0.4); }

components.name: Trust Badge
components.description: Pill-shaped live-status badge with a pulsing dot, used in the public hero.
components.html: Disponible maintenant
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.2); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); } .ds-badge-dot-wrap { position: relative; display: flex; height: 8px; width: 8px; } .ds-badge-ping { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: #34d399; opacity: 0.75; animation: ds-ping 1s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-badge-dot { position: relative; display: inline-flex; border-radius: 9999px; height: 8px; width: 8px; background: #10b981; } .ds-badge-text { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.9); } @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview: Leviosa runs two surfaces on one token system today, and they're headed in different directions. The staff/admin/client dashboard is a plain, traditional working tool — it stays that way; no branding ambition needed there. The public storefront is where the effort goes: booking should feel as frictionless as Doctolib, but the brand voice is shifting from "calm wellness portal" toward something with more edge — professional and trustworthy enough to hand over your time and payment, but confident and current rather than sedate, closer to a streetwear campaign than a spa brochure. The tokens extracted are the honest baseline as they exist in code right now: a near-grayscale neutral system (true zinc/charcoal, not a warm-tinted "AI cream") with a pale sky-blue accent and functional red/green/amber. The public hero already leans bolder than pure "calm" — full-bleed video, dark overlay, oversized type — but the rest of the storefront still reads soft and restrained. Closing that gap toward "The Studio Drop" energy is active brand work, not yet finished.
keyCharacteristics: True neutral grayscale (zinc-derived), not a warm/cream-tinted 'AI default' base
One functional accent (pale sky blue) used sparingly, not as a brand color
Soft, tactile elevation: gentle shadows and rounded corners (9-20px) everywhere
Admin/staff dashboard: traditional, utilitarian, unbranded by design
Public storefront: currently restrained; directionally moving toward bolder, more energetic branding

rules.name: The Function-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Outside of Ink and Paper, every color in this system maps to a state (error, success, warning, subtle highlight) — never to decoration.

rules.name: The One Display Rule
rules.body: Cal Sans is loaded in a single weight and appears only at section-heading scale — never body copy, never buttons.

rules.name: The Escalation-On-Interaction Rule
rules.body: Interactive elements start at shadow-mini or shadow-card at rest and escalate to shadow-popover plus a slight scale on hover — never the reverse.

dos: Do keep Ink + Paper as the load-bearing pair; let Sky/Rose/Green/Amber stay strictly functional.
Do use Cal Sans sparingly, at heading scale only.
Do escalate shadow + scale together on hover/interactive states.
Do treat the staff/admin/client dashboard as a plain, traditional tool.
Do keep the booking flow the least-decorated, fastest path in the whole product.
donts: Don't introduce a warm cream/sand/beige base.
Don't let the public storefront settle for 'calm and welcoming' as the finished brand.
Don't carry new branding effort into the staff/admin/client dashboard.
Don't use a generic clinical/healthcare-portal look or a generic corporate-SaaS-marketing look.
Don't use border-left/right accent stripes, gradient text, or decorative glassmorphism outside the one deliberate trust-badge use.
